title: The World's Most Rewarding Wildlife Travel Experiences
paragraphs: You might have seen animals like gorillas and penguins in the zoo, but it's not the same as encountering them in their natural habitat.
However, getting to that habitat can be difficult — and some animals are so rare that, even if you go there, you may not see them.
So if you're desperate to travel to see an animal in its natural habitat, which trips are the best?

British travel company Bailey Robinson ranked 30 wildlife travel experiences based on how rare the animals are, how hard it is to reach their habitat, and how likely you are to encounter them once you're there. They also tried to avoid the common African safari experiences, like seeing lions and elephants.
At the top of the list is seeing mountain gorillas in Rwanda or Uganda.

Mountain gorillas are very rare, with just over 1,000 left in the world. But local guides know where to find them — though few visitors are allowed to come along. There are only two or three dozen groups of gorillas that can be visited, and just eight tourists are allowed to visit each group in a day.

In second place on Bailey Robinson's list is an expedition to see emperor penguins in Antarctica. While there are about 600,000 adult emperor penguins in Antarctica, their numbers have been declining — and it's certainly hard to get to Antarctica to see them there!

In third place is seeing saiga antelopes in Kazakhstan. A symbol of the region's steppes, these large-nosed animals travel up to 1,000 kilometers between summer and winter. Their numbers dropped as low as 21,000 in the early 2000s, but there are about 3 million in the wild today.
The rest of the top 10 includes tracking snow leopards in the Himalayas, finding the Javan rhinoceros in Indonesia, and seeing polar bears in Svalbard, a Norwegian archipelago in the Arctic Ocean.
